title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #18

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A gourd rattle makes sound because (1 mark)
   A. a bow is rubbed
   B. the seeds inside knock against the walls
   C. air is blown through it
   D. strings are plucked

2. What does the drumhead do when it is struck? (1 mark)
   A. It stays completely still
   B. It holds the drum stand
   C. It vibrates and makes the sound
   D. It cools the drum

3. Claves are (1 mark)
   A. a horn
   B. two wooden sticks hit together
   C. drums with strings
   D. a kind of flute

4. What is the minimum distance a defender must keep from the player with the ball? (1 mark)
   A. 10 metres
   B. 1 centimetre
   C. 5 metres
   D. 0.9 metres

5. A full netball court is divided into how many equal parts? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Three
   C. Six
   D. Two

6. Overlapping in a montage means (1 mark)
   A. pieces are painted black
   B. pieces are far apart
   C. one piece partly covers another
   D. pieces are cut into tiny bits

7. Which of these is a dark tone of red? (1 mark)
   A. Red mixed with a little black
   B. Red mixed with white
   C. Red mixed with water
   D. Red mixed with yellow

8. Rhythm is (1 mark)
   A. the pattern of long and short sounds
   B. the name of the song
   C. the loudness of the singer
   D. how high a note is

9. Which pattern has three beats of sound and one beat of silence? (1 mark)
   A. taa taa taa (rest)
   B. (rest) (rest) (rest) (rest)
   C. taa taa taa taa
   D. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te

10. The middle note of d, r and m is (1 mark)
   A. none
   B. d
   C. m
   D. r

11. The sol-fa syllable r is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. ree
   B. rah
   C. roh
   D. ray

12. How can you make a slab of even thickness? (1 mark)
   A. Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   B. Freeze it
   C. Drop it on the floor
   D. Squeeze with one hand

13. Which move is a step? (1 mark)
   A. m to d in one jump over r
   B. d to m
   C. d to d
   D. d to r

14. Which is a sprint distance in big athletics competitions? (1 mark)
   A. 10 000 metres
   B. Marathon
   C. 100 metres
   D. Half marathon

15. How far apart are the hands placed at the start? (1 mark)
   A. One on each side of the track
   B. Touching each other
   C. As far as possible
   D. Shoulder-width apart

16. What happens on the command set? (1 mark)
   A. The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   B. The runners sit
   C. The race ends
   D. The runners run

17. What is patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of race
   B. Fear of runners
   C. Love of food
   D. Love for one's country

18. Why do we warm up before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. To make the mat softer
   B. To learn songs
   C. To prepare the muscles and joints
   D. To make us tired

19. In a crab balance, your body is supported by (1 mark)
   A. the head only
   B. the back only
   C. the knees and elbows
   D. both hands and both feet

20. What should you do if something hurts during gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Keep going
   B. Hide it
   C. Stop and tell your teacher
   D. Push a friend

21. What should you do with long hair in gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Tie it back
   B. Let it hang in your face
   C. Cover the mat with it
   D. Cut it during class

22. What is a spotter or supporting partner's job? (1 mark)
   A. To leave
   B. To laugh
   C. To help gently as your teacher shows you
   D. To push you

23. A folk song is (1 mark)
   A. a song without a message
   B. a traditional song belonging to a community
   C. a song only for cities
   D. a computer song

24. Which folk songs welcome a new baby? (1 mark)
   A. Funeral songs
   B. Naming songs
   C. Work songs
   D. Initiation songs

25. The element of light means (1 mark)
   A. the size of the photo
   B. how well the subject is lit
   C. the weight of the camera
   D. the price

26. What should you do before photographing someone? (1 mark)
   A. Ask their permission
   B. Take it secretly
   C. Take photos of strangers only
   D. Shout at them

27. For a well-lit photograph of a person, the sun should be (1 mark)
   A. under the ground
   B. behind the person
   C. behind the photographer
   D. inside the lens

28. How many joints does a descant recorder have? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Three
   C. Five
   D. Six

29. Why keep a recorder away from strong sun and fire? (1 mark)
   A. Heat can bend it
   B. The sun makes it sing
   C. It becomes lighter
   D. It becomes invisible

30. Why should you not use very hot water on a plastic recorder? (1 mark)
   A. It makes it play higher
   B. It makes it louder
   C. It can bend the plastic
   D. It makes it heavier

31. The song Hot Cross Buns can be played on (1 mark)
   A. C D E only
   B. B A G
   C. only G and C
   D. only drums

32. Which hand is at the top of the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Right
   B. Left
   C. Both feet
   D. Neither

33. What helps your body to float? (1 mark)
   A. Being heavy
   B. Kicking hard only
   C. Holding a stone
   D. Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air

34. In a glide, your face is (1 mark)
   A. hidden by a hat
   B. in the water with the head between your arms
   C. high above the water
   D. turned to the side always

35. Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should (1 mark)
   A. swim alone
   B. only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   C. go in at night
   D. dive from rocks

36. A hare hop suits a rhythm that is (1 mark)
   A. very slow
   B. quick like ta-te ta-te
   C. absent
   D. silent

37. The Kenya National Anthem is a (1 mark)
   A. a game
   B. national symbol
   C. a work song
   D. a topical song about washing

38. Which is a component of a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. Community of origin
   B. Weight
   C. Price
   D. Distance

39. Every displayed work should have (1 mark)
   A. a price only
   B. a secret code
   C. no name
   D. a label with the title and artist's name

40. Sportsmanship means (1 mark)
   A. teasing others
   B. cheating to win
   C. hitting
   D. being fair and kind in sports

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three hygiene rules for the pool. (3 marks)

42. Why is it important to appreciate the percussion instruments of different communities? (3 marks)

43. State the lengths of a crotchet rest and a quaver rest and how to show a rest when clapping. (3 marks)

44. How many beats are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa taa? Show your working. (3 marks)

45. Give three ways of storing and handling a recorder safely. (3 marks)

46. Give three responsible ways of using a device for photography. (3 marks)

47. Describe how to make a chest pass. (4 marks)

48. Explain how to compose a short melody using d, r and m. (4 marks)

49. Why should you delete poor photographs from a device? (3 marks)

50. Describe how to paint the Kenyan flag on paper. (5 marks)

51. What are the sol-fa syllables for the three notes learned, and which is the lowest? (2 marks)

52. Describe the fingering for B, A and G. (3 marks)

53. Describe the position of the back knee in the medium start and in the elongated start. (3 marks)

54. State three mistakes in gliding and how to correct them. (3 marks)

55. Explain the difference between the prone float and the supine float. (3 marks)

56. Describe the steps of a glide. (4 marks)

57. Describe how to do the side roll safely. (4 marks)

58. What is a balance in gymnastics? (2 marks)

59. What is a montage? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — the seeds inside knock against the walls
   When shaken, seeds inside hit the gourd and make a sound.

2. C — It vibrates and makes the sound
   The stretched skin shakes very fast and produces sound.

3. B — two wooden sticks hit together
   Claves are two hardwood sticks that are struck together.

4. D — 0.9 metres
   A defender must stand at least 0.9 metres away.

5. B — Three
   A netball court is divided into three equal thirds.

6. C — one piece partly covers another
   Overlapping helps to fill gaps and make the montage full.

7. A — Red mixed with a little black
   Adding black makes a darker shade of red.

8. A — the pattern of long and short sounds
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds over the beat.

9. A — taa taa taa (rest)
   Only the first has a single rest and three sounding beats.

10. D — r
   Ray lies between doh and me.

11. D — ray
   The syllable r is ray.

12. A — Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   Equal sticks on both sides keep the slab even.

13. D — d to r
   Doh to ray is to the next note.

14. C — 100 metres
   The sprints are 100 m, 200 m and 400 m.

15. D — Shoulder-width apart
   Hands are about shoulder-width apart.

16. A — The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   On set, runners lift the hips and hold still.

17. D — Love for one's country
   Patriotism is love and respect for one's country.

18. C — To prepare the muscles and joints
   A warm body is less likely to be injured.

19. D — both hands and both feet
   A crab balance rests on two hands and two feet.

20. C — Stop and tell your teacher
   Pain is a warning, so stop and tell the teacher.

21. A — Tie it back
   Tied-back hair does not get in your way.

22. C — To help gently as your teacher shows you
   A partner supports carefully and only in the way taught.

23. B — a traditional song belonging to a community
   Folk songs are passed on by singing.

24. B — Naming songs
   Naming songs are sung when a baby is named.

25. B — how well the subject is lit
   Light is a key element.

26. A — Ask their permission
   Permission is polite and safe.

27. C — behind the photographer
   Light falls on the front of the subject.

28. B — Three
   Head joint, middle joint and foot joint.

29. A — Heat can bend it
   Heat can warp or crack the instrument.

30. C — It can bend the plastic
   Heat can warp plastic.

31. B — B A G
   It uses the three notes B, A and G.

32. B — Left
   The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom.

33. D — Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   Buoyancy and air in the lungs.

34. B — in the water with the head between your arms
   Keeping the face in helps the body stay level.

35. B — only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   Open water is more dangerous.

36. B — quick like ta-te ta-te
   Hares hop quickly.

37. B — national symbol
   Like the flag, it stands for the nation.

38. A — Community of origin
   Components include community, type, message, participants and instruments.

39. D — a label with the title and artist's name
   Labels help viewers.

40. D — being fair and kind in sports
   It includes following rules and respecting others.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Shower before and after; do not spit or pass urine in the pool; do not drink the water; dry yourself and change into dry clothes. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show the culture and skill of each community. They help us respect one another. They should be preserved for future generations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet rest is one beat of silence and a quaver rest is half a beat of silence. When clapping, we do not clap but keep the beat silently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each length, 1 mark for showing the rest.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 beats. Ta-te is 1 beat, ta-te is 1 beat, taa is 1 beat and taa is 1 beat, so 1+1+1+1 = 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it in a bag or case; keep away from heat; do not drop it; twist joints gently; do not bite it. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before photographing someone; do not photograph in private places; do not share photographs without permission; use it only for the set task. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold the ball at chest height with both hands. Look at the partner. Step forward and straighten the arms, turning the thumbs down. The ball goes to the partner's chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give a syllable to each note. Use steps. End on d as a crotchet. Sing it and show the hand signs. Write the syllables under the rhythm names.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: To save memory space, keep only good pictures and make it easier to find the best ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Cut a rectangle of paper in the ratio three to two. Draw the stripes and the thin white lines lightly with a ruler. Sketch the shield and the crossed spears in the middle. Paint black at the top, red in the middle and green at the bottom, leaving the white lines. Let it dry and attach it to a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the rectangle, drawing stripes, shield, colour order and drying with handle.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: d, r and m. d is the lowest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming, 1 mark for the lowest.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each note.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: In the medium start, the back knee is level with the middle of the front foot. In the elongated start it is level with the heel of the front foot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position, 1 mark for saying the elongated start is further back.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting the head: keep it between the arms; bent arms or legs: stretch them; pushing too hard: push gently. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prone is face down in the water with arms stretched forward. Supine is on the back with the face up and ears in the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each float, 1 mark for the difference.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stand with the back to the wall and arms stretched overhead. Put the feet on the wall and bend the knees. Take a breath and put the face in. Push off gently with the body straight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lie on the back with body straight. Stretch the arms overhead with palms together and legs together. Tighten the tummy and point the toes. Roll over on to the side and tummy in a straight line. Get up slowly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: A position held still for a few seconds under control.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for still position, 1 mark for control or holding.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A picture made by joining many cut pictures or pieces of material on a background.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many pieces, 1 mark for joined on a background.
